points: MP Aleksandr Fediyenko stated approximately two million draft dodgers remain invisible to the state, urging creation of detection conditions before assessing mobilization resources. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/32313)
Zelensky's advisor "Flash" warned Ukrainians to buy batteries and power equipment now, predicting prices will double or triple in coming months as winter approaches. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/32339)

Achilles Brigade seeks electronics repair specialists for FPV drone workshop in rear positions, requiring SMD soldering, schematic reading, and service center experience, offering 50,000 UAH and mobilization deferment. (Source: @DeepStateUA/23729)
Zelensky emphasized Ukraine will receive powerful US security guarantees post-war and has no intention of leaving Donbas or abandoning its people. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/32315)
In Odesa, Territorial Recruitment Center employees forcibly detained a man in his underwear, reflecting ongoing mobilization tensions. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/32319)

GUR Deputy Chief Vadym Skibitsky reported Russian missile production at 110-120% of plan: July record 198 ballistic missiles (Iskander-M, S-400, Zircon), Kh-101 at 140% (87 vs 72 planned), Kalibr at 111% (29), annual Zircon (33) and Onyx (60) quotas met by early August. (Source: @eRadarrua/104769)

Russia paused Kinzhal and Kh-32 production since April, redirecting resources to more accurate ballistics and anti-ship Kh-35 (plan exceeded 2x), while accumulating missiles for autumn-winter energy infrastructure strikes. (Source: @eRadarrua/104769)

Russian veterans in Yessentuki, Stavropol Krai, announced formation of private security structure after locals beat a "SVO hero" to death, indicating internal friction among war participants. (Source: @eRadarrua/104796)

Deputy FM Mikhail Galuzin warned armed provocations by Kiev and Moldovan authorities against Transnistria will be regarded as attack on Russia, while accusing Chisinau of following Brussels' anti-Russian directives. (Source: @tass_agency/389595, @tass_agency/389591)
Syria and Russia agreed to convert Russian military bases in Syria into joint training centers, with civilian Russian assets transferred to Syrian state management. (Source: @UkraineNow/83327)

DeepState map update shows enemy advanced near Sukhetske in Donetsk region, with fundraiser for 46th Separate Amphibious Assault Brigade collecting 50% for optical cables for drones. (Source: @DeepStateUA/23728)
Jet UAV launched from Donbas toward Kharkiv region, course set for Lozova, indicating continued aerial pressure on eastern logistics hubs. (Source: @kpszsu/72285)

Ukrainian July strikes targeted 14 bridges and crossings in occupied Donetsk, Luhansk, Kherson, Zaporizhzhia regions and Crimea, complicating Russian troop and ammunition transfers. (Source: @UkraineNow/83343)

At least nine Russian air defense and EW systems destroyed in July including S-400, Buk, Pantsir-S2, and Murmansk-BN complexes across eastern and southern occupied territories. (Source: @UkraineNow/83343)

Multiple jet UAVs launched from Bryansk region, Russia, toward Chernihiv region targeting Snovsk, Horodnia, and Mena, with additional reactive UAV detected near Zaporizhzhia near Georgiivske. (Source: @eRadarrua/104805, @kpszsu/72280, @eRadarrua/104798)
Ballistic missile strike reported on Chernihiv city, with additional threat of Iskander-M/S-300 launches from Kursk region per air defense monitoring. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/70025, @mon1tor_ua/70035)

Several UAVs detected in northern Sumy region on courses toward Novhorod-Siverskyi, Konotop, Shostka, and Velyki Sorochyntsi (Poltava region), with reactive UAV groups active in western Sumy region. (Source: @kpszsu/72277, @kpszsu/72281, @kpszsu/72276, @kpszsu/72265, @eRadarrua/104765)
Russian Tu-22M3 bomber from Olenya airfield operating in Black Sea waters, posing Kh-22 missile launch threat to northern and central Ukraine. (Source: @eRadarrua/104784)

Kh-59 missiles targeted Zatoka in Odesa region, while jet UAVs from Black Sea approached Tatarbunary (Odesa region) and Shaheds struck Zaporizhzhia city. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/70019, @kpszsu/72284, @kpszsu/72288, @mon1tor_ua/70022)

UAV from Kherson region directed toward Snihurivka (Mykolaiv region), with reactive UAV through Kherson region toward Bashtanka (Mykolaiv region) and Shahed from Kirovohrad region toward Bashkansky district (Mykolaiv region). (Source: @kpszsu/72250, @kpszsu/72258, @mon1tor_ua/70021)

Ukrainian July strikes destroyed fuel infrastructure including Kerch terminal, Shakhtarsk fuel depot, and a tanker in Black Sea, plus hangars at Saki and Gvardeyskoye airfields in Crimea. (Source: @UkraineNow/83343)

Over ten UAV control points, drone warehouses, and an FSB center in Kherson region hit in July, degrading Russian reconnaissance-strike complexes in southern occupied territories. (Source: @UkraineNow/83343)
Zaporizhzhia region suffered five KAB strikes on civilian infrastructure with at least five injured, per regional military administration. (Source: @UkraineNow/83329)

Russia transitioning to Geran-4 and Geran-5 Shahed variants with turbojet engines, harder for mobile air defense groups to intercept, while integrating Mesh networks for online control and testing "Rassvet" Starlink analog. (Source: @eRadarrua/104769)

Russian "Rassvet" satellite constellation currently operates fragmentarily when satellites pass over Ukraine; plans for 292 satellites by 2027 and 924 by 2035 to achieve full Starlink-like capability. (Source: @UkraineNow/83336)

Global Patriot missile stockpile decreased from 2,200 to under 827, THAAD from 452 to under 278 (CSIS data), as US defense companies resist licensing production to Ukraine citing intellectual property concerns. (Source: @UkraineNow/83331)

Ukrainian July campaign destroyed at least nine Russian AD/EW systems: S-400, Buk, Pantsir-S2, Murmansk-BN, plus over ten UAV control points, significantly degrading Russian air defense coverage. (Source: @UkraineNow/83343)

Four Shaheds from Poltava region toward Zolotonosha district (Cherkasy region), three Shaheds toward Zaporizhzhia, one reactive Shahed circling near Kryvyi Rih (Dnipropetrovsk region), one Shahed toward Shostka (Sumy region). (Source: @mon1tor_ua/70022, @mon1tor_ua/70021)

sections.threat_assessment: Russian missile production surge to 110-120% of plan with record July output of 198 ballistic missiles indicates sustained high-intensity strike capacity through autumn-winter, specifically targeting energy infrastructure. Deployment of turbojet-powered Geran-4/5 Shaheds with Mesh network integration and advancing "Rassvet" satellite constellation will significantly challenge Ukrainian mobile air defenses and electronic warfare. Ukrainian deep strikes like Tyumen (2,000+ km) demonstrate expanding reach against strategic economic targets, while systematic degradation of Russian AD/EW systems (9+ in July) and logistics bridges (14) creates cumulative operational pressure. However, Ukraine's mobilization crisis with ~2 million undetected draft evaders and winter energy vulnerability pose serious domestic sustainability risks.
sections.regional_response: Serbia maintained refusal to impose sanctions on Russia despite Zelensky's visit, with President Vučić confirming unchanged policy. Poland saw protests in 22 cities against violence toward Ukrainians, delivering 11,000+ signature petition to Prime Minister's Office and Interior Ministry demanding decisive action. Moldova faces Russian diplomatic pressure as Deputy FM Galuzin frames any Transnistria-related actions as attacks on Russia, while accusing Chisinau of following Brussels' anti-Russian directives. US defense industry resists Patriot missile licensing to Ukraine citing intellectual property, even as global stockpiles plummet below 827 Patriots and 278 THAAD interceptors.
sections.intelligence_notes: Russian shift from Kinzhal/Kh-32 to mass-produced ballistic and anti-ship missiles suggests tactical adaptation for saturation attacks on Ukrainian air defenses. Ukrainian "middle strike" concept of simultaneous EW, fuel, bridge, and UAV control point targeting shows matured operational art for cumulative effect. Russian veteran self-organization in Stavropol after killing of "SVO hero" indicates potential domestic instability vectors. Achilles Brigade's recruitment of civilian electronics specialists for FPV repair reflects Ukraine's growing reliance on technical talent mobilization in rear areas. German journalist incident at Belgrade press conference highlights escalating information warfare and historical sensitivities in European discourse.
